mechanism: Both are NSAIDs; concurrent use increases bleeding risk and may reduce aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
plain_english: Taking aspirin and ibuprofen together increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Avoid combining them unless your doctor specifically advises it.

mechanism: Concurrent NSAID use; additive GI bleeding and ulceration risk.
plain_english: Using aspirin and naproxen together can irritate your stomach lining and increase bleeding risk. Consult your doctor before taking both.

mechanism: Additive antiplatelet and GI bleeding effects.
plain_english: Aspirin and diclofenac together can increase the chance of stomach bleeding. Use only if your doctor recommends it.

mechanism: Additive NSAID toxicity: GI bleeding, renal impairment.
plain_english: Combining two pain-relief anti-inflammatory medicines like ibuprofen and diclofenac raises the risk of stomach and kidney problems.

mechanism: Two NSAIDs: additive GI and renal toxicity.
plain_english: Taking ibuprofen and naproxen at the same time provides no extra benefit but doubles the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain.

mechanism: NSAIDs can reduce renal blood flow, decreasing metformin excretion and raising lactic acidosis risk.
plain_english: Ibuprofen may affect how your kidneys clear metformin. Short-term use is usually fine, but monitor for any unusual fatigue or stomach pain.

mechanism: NSAID-related reduction in renal clearance of metformin.
plain_english: Diclofenac can slow down how your body removes metformin. Let your doctor know if you feel unusually tired or nauseous.

mechanism: Omeprazole may slightly increase azithromycin plasma levels via CYP3A4 inhibition.
plain_english: Omeprazole may cause a small increase in azithromycin levels. This is usually harmless, but report any new irregular heartbeat to your doctor.

mechanism: Mutual CYP3A4 inhibition; both drugs increase each other's plasma levels.
plain_english: Clarithromycin and omeprazole can each raise the level of the other in your blood. This is generally manageable — your doctor may have prescribed them together intentionally.

mechanism: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium bind ciprofloxacin in the gut, reducing antibiotic absorption by up to 90%.
plain_english: Antacids can stop your body from absorbing ciprofloxacin properly. Take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after any antacid.

mechanism: Chelation of ciprofloxacin by divalent cations reduces absorption.
plain_english: Magnesium-based antacids block ciprofloxacin from being absorbed. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

mechanism: Divalent/trivalent cations chelate tetracyclines, reducing absorption.
plain_english: Antacids reduce the absorption of doxycycline. Take doxycycline 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacid use.

mechanism: Chelation reduces doxycycline bioavailability.
plain_english: Magnesium antacids can block doxycycline from working. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

mechanism: Additive CNS depression; combined sedation may be stronger than expected.
plain_english: Tramadol and cetirizine can both cause drowsiness. Together, you may feel more tired or light-headed than usual — avoid driving.

mechanism: Additive CNS depression and increased seizure risk.
plain_english: Tramadol and chlorpheniramine together can cause significant drowsiness and, rarely, increase seizure risk. Avoid driving or operating machinery.

mechanism: Additive CNS sedation.
plain_english: Both medicines can cause drowsiness — the effect may be stronger when used together. Take care when driving.

mechanism: Additive CNS depression.
plain_english: Codeine and cetirizine both cause drowsiness. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while taking them together.

mechanism: Amoxicillin reduces methotrexate renal clearance, risking toxicity.
plain_english: Amoxicillin can cause methotrexate levels to build up dangerously in your body. Tell your doctor immediately if both are prescribed.

mechanism: Alcohol increases lactic acidosis risk with metformin.
plain_english: Drinking alcohol while taking metformin increases the risk of a serious condition called lactic acidosis. Avoid alcohol or limit it strictly.

mechanism: Additive anticoagulation and antiplatelet effect; major bleeding risk.
plain_english: Aspirin with warfarin greatly increases the risk of serious bleeding. Only take them together if your doctor specifically prescribes it.

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and reduces conversion of clopidogrel to its active form.
plain_english: Omeprazole may reduce how well clopidogrel works to prevent blood clots. If you are on clopidogrel, ask your doctor about a different antacid.

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce methotrexate renal clearance, risking haematological toxicity.
plain_english: Ibuprofen can cause methotrexate to accumulate to dangerous levels. Do not combine these without close medical supervision.
